newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close off 1.61 pct on trade jitters.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close off 1.61 pct on trade jitters.

text.p: Brazil shares ended off 1.61 percent on concerns over Brazil's increasing trade deficit, which is projected to grow as much as $1.0 billion in October, traders said.

"We are worried about the country's (macroeconomic) situation. If foreign direct investment stops coming to Brazil, our situation will become worrisome," said Evandro dos Reis Junior, trader at Indusval brokerage house.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares closed down 1,071 points at 65,596 points. Turnover was moderate at 365.7 million reais ($ 355.2 million).
Nervousness over trade hit the stock market as well as the foreign exchange market, where the real closed at 1.0296 per dollar, down 0.11 percent.

According to brokers, uneasiness in both markets grew after Central Bank chief Gustavo Loyola told reporters in New York that the bank did not have any plans to tighten monetary policy or speed the real's depreciation to lower the trade deficit.
They said Loyola's remarks fueled speculation in the market because in the past the Central Bank has done the opposite of what it said it would do.
Profit-taking was strong in bellwether Telebras preferred reais.

Telebras receipts, which trade at a discount in the secondary market, rose 3.42 percent to close at 46 reais on continued speculation that a Brazilian court could rule that Telebras must transform the receipts into shares at a later date.

Power firm Electrobras preferred shares ended up 0.61 percent at 328 reais. Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred shares closed at 20.35 reais, down 1.21 percent. Oil monopoly Petrobras preferred shares fell 2.71 percent to close at 125.50 reais.

Brazilian bank Bamerindus common shares ended slightly up 0.06 percent at 17.46 reais on local press reports that investment banks Pactual and Icatu were the most likely candidates for managing finances of the troubled bank and ready it for sale. A Bamerindus spokesman said he could not comment on the report.
Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index comprising nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector (IEE) fell 0.46 percent to close at 1,766 points, a bourse spokeswoman said.
